direction.comments: SPOILER-WARNING; the direction on a macroscale is pretty good overall, as Iñárritu shows why he is a two-time Best Director winner by seamlessly weaving the fake narrative of the play together with the actual narrative, building the real world and its stakes very well, along with how the characters were impacted by it and the production going on behind the play; however, the play itself very much tries to be Dr. Strangelove, a satire so over the top that it becomes a mocking caricature of not only the world the movie is set in, but also where the real world might be heading because of the government, the Trump administration, and AI-integrated technology, which makes it feel fake and so hard to get through, and while the reveal that it is a play kind of feels like an excuse to cover up those flaws, they are still very much visible; the direction on a microscale is very good for the actual story, as all the actors know what they are doing and deliver very emotional performances that show the stakes, pressure, weight of the world, and personal conflicts with good chemistry, but the play is so hard to get through because it is such an over-the-top copycat of Dr. Strangelove that it gets bogged down by how much of a chaotic mess it is; the storytelling is good, setting your expectations in the first 30 minutes so you think the movie is going to suck before subverting them with the reveal that it is a play, then weaving between the two sides of the movie well to show why the play is being made about what actually happened, alongside subplots like Tom Cruise's character caring about his daughter; the tension is built well once you find out what the movie is actually about and what the stakes are

performance.comments: His return to prestige films shows why he is such a great actor as he brings real depth to the actor he plays in the actual story, feeling like a well-seasoned actor and a father dealing with the stakes of his daughter being gone, and he really brings to life Digger Rockwell in the play as he builds a comedic, over-the-top caricature of a man that is truly scary; has good chemistry with the cast in the actual story, especially Sophie Wilde, but doesn't have the best chemistry with the cast in the play as it is just a little too over-the-top and bad
While he is intentionally bad and over-the-top to mimic how satirical the play is, I genuinely found his performance a bit annoying and way more of a caricature than a believable character

Basically plays an over-the-top caricature of a President Trump-like character that is pretty hard to judge because of how intentionally bad he's supposed to be; the non-play scenes he is given are pretty decent
Honestly isn't given that much to work with, and her performance is just barely over-the-top
Plays very much a lackey VP character similar to JD Vance that feels over-the-top and satirical of the current administration

I genuinely really enjoyed his performance as he does not have to deal with the flaws of the play part of the movie and can bring a lot of depth to his character in the real world as he shows a deep connection to the play; has pretty good chemistry with Cruise

The best performance outside of Tom Cruise as she is very dynamic and shows the stress of running a big-scale production; shows a wide range of emotions and is very dynamic in her delivery and demeanor; has very good chemistry with Tom Cruise

cast.comments: All the actors know what they are doing, delivering very emotional performances in the actual story that show the stakes, pressure, weight of the world, and personal conflicts, with good chemistry in this part of the movie, but the play's performances are just such intentionally over-the-top caricatures of real-life figures that they honestly are just not good and are hard to get through

story.comments: SPOILER-WARNING; the concept is genuinely great, using a fake play to subvert your expectations before leading into an actual story about them reenacting the events in the movie's world through that play, which creates a meta critique of the real world both through the play and through the actual story of the movie that critiques the play, and it surprised me since I went in very skeptical because of all the negative press and trailers; the plot structure is good and bad, as the first 30 minutes are a chore to get through, but once you know what the movie is about, the way it weaves between the real world and the play is very good and builds to a climax where you see the stakes and how much everything is impacting the characters; however, it focuses way too much on the play after the reveal, and since you have already established that these moments are intentionally over the top and satirical, there is no reason to have us sit through them for so long, so while you can't cut the beginning because it sets up the reveal, trimming 10 to 15 minutes of the play from the middle would still get the point across without having us sit through this chore of an intentionally bad play, especially when you are just wishing to get back to the real world because it is a genuinely well-made movie; character writing for Digger is a caricature of a man who did serious harm in the world of the movie, played for laughs but emblematic of different real-world figures, while the actor Tom Cruise plays actually has depth, feeling like a well-seasoned actor and a father dealing with the stakes of his daughter being gone, but the rest of the characters in the play are caricatures of real-life figures that are a little too over the top and so on the nose, with the president clearly being Trump surrounded by his vice president, cabinet, and evangelical yes men, that it feels like beating a dead horse, since I'm not going to learn anything new about this administration when I'm living through it right now, though it could be a good time capsule in 10 to 15 years if things change

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is a tale of two movies: it is well written for the actual movie as it is profound and carries the emotional weight, stakes, and personal conflicts of what is actually going on, but the play is intentionally written to be over-the-top and satirical, like a Dr. Strangelove copycat, but it just plays way too much into being intentionally bad, to the point that it feels more like a chore than funny; the movie tries way too hard to be funny as an over-the-top satire, with a pretty low hit rate as I would say it only hits 1 in 5 times, as even though I think this movie is very much a comedy, it is better commentary than it is a comedy; the symbolism is strong as a meta critique, with the play mocking the world the movie is set in while the movie uses it to critique where the real world might be heading with the government, the Trump administration, and AI-integrated technology, though it is so on the nose that it feels like beating a dead horse; the symbolism for the movie is better in the actual movie than it is in the play; the foreshadowing is built around the reveal, as the intentionally bad first 30 minutes set you up to think the movie is going to suck before subverting your expectations once you find out it is a play

score.comments: The score is used sparingly in this movie, and when it is used, it is used for tones, tension, and transitions

cinematography.comments: The true highlight for this movie as Lubezki shows why he is one of the greatest cinematographers of all time; the use of wide-angle shots and VistaVision in the play makes the movie feel very Dr. Strangelove-esque; the cinematography in the actual movie is well shot and makes the movie feel very much like a combination of Birdman and The Revenant with its shot selection and darker tones

editing.comments: Well edited and choreographed together from a stitch perspective as the movie seamlessly goes between the play and actual movie very well; from a cut perspective, this movie really could have trimmed 10 to 15 minutes of the play after the reveal happens

visual_effects.comments: Objectively bad and cheap; while I do understand you can argue that this adds to the intentionally bad moments of the movie, the visual effects are just genuinely not good and feel very fake (especially for a big-budget movie like this)

production_design.comments: The set design is very good for this movie as they are able to go between these handcrafted sets for the play that make it feel larger than life and very Dr. Strangelove-esque, and the set design for the actual story makes it feel pretty dystopian

makeup.comments: Truly transforms Tom Cruise into Digger Rockwell as it is a key reason why this movie works as it creates this caricature of capitalism; the makeup for the rest of the characters is good too as it helps create these other caricatures for the play

costumes.comments: Helps transform these characters into caricatures of the real world, especially Digger Rockwell

review.pacing: Slowed down by how much time it spends on the fake story they advertised, as the first 30 minutes are genuinely unbearable, and even after the reveal, the play scenes go on for way too long and feel like a chore to sit through before getting back to the good stuff in the actual story, so trimming 10 to 15 minutes of the play after the reveal would have made it much tighter
review.climax: Ends very well, bringing the weaving between the play and the actual story to a climax where you see the stakes and how much everything is impacting the characters
review.tone: A tale of two movies, with the play being an intentionally bad, over-the-top Dr. Strangelove-esque satire, while the actual story is darker and pretty dystopian, feeling like a combination of Birdman and The Revenant
review.final_notes: This movie is very much what Beau Is Afraid should have been
review.overall: Overall, whenever people say a movie is either the best or the worst movie ever, I'm always in between, and 'Digger' is no different; it is really a movie of two different parts (SPOILER-WARNING), as the actual story is genuinely great and well written, carried by Lubezki's beautiful cinematography and Tom Cruise's return to prestige filmmaking, but the movie focuses way too much on this over-the-top satirical play that feels like a chore to get through; while you cannot change the movie before the reveal happens, if you cut 10 to 15 minutes of the play after this moment, the movie would go from a 7/10 to an 8/10
